title: Connected fibres of proper chains under two-branch pinching
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C,W\to S$ be projective flat finitely presented families with nodal geometric curve fibres [def-kun-projective, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $B,N$ be finite etale $S$-schemes and $B\to N$ finite etale of constant degree two [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Supply closed immersions $B\hookrightarrow C$ and $B\hookrightarrow W$ into their relative smooth loci [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $h:W\to C$ carries these immersions to one another and factors as a finite chain $W=V_m\to\cdots\to V_0=C$ of proper morphisms with nonempty geometrically connected fibres [def-weil-proper-morphism]. This means each fibre stays nonempty and connected after every field extension of its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Length zero and empty $B,N$ are allowed. Let $X=C\amalg_BN$ and $Y=W\amalg_BN$ be the scheme pushouts [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], assumed projective over $S$, with both squares cartesian, finite surjective curve-to-pushout maps, closed immersions from $N$, complement isomorphisms $C\setminus B\cong X\setminus N$ and $W\setminus B\cong Y\setminus N$, and pushout squares remaining pushouts after base change to every geometric fibre [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion], and let $p:Y\to X$ be induced by $h$ and the identity of $N$. Then $h$ and $p$ are proper with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. For every geometric point $\bar s\to S$, if $X_{\bar s}$ is nonempty and connected, so is $Y_{\bar s}$. No connectedness of $C_{\bar s}$, $W_{\bar s}$ or the intermediate $V_{j,\bar s}$ is assumed. Here nodal geometric curve fibres are nonempty reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one whose nonsmooth closed points over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ have completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$; they may be disconnected [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Agent connected-fibre consequence of Tag 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral), quotient topology and geometric branch pinching; old common-model step 10, including closed-image composition for proper chains.

proof.text: Composition gives properness of $h$ (the identity if $m=0$). Projectivity gives properness of $X,Y$ over $S$, and hence separatedness of $X/S$. The induced $S$-morphism $p:Y\to X$ is therefore proper by proper-over-separated.

Fix any field-valued point $c:\operatorname{Spec}L\to C$. Put $F_j=V_j\times_C\operatorname{Spec}L$. We prove $F_j$ nonempty connected by induction, starting with $F_0=\operatorname{Spec}L$. The map $F_j\to F_{j-1}$ is a base change of the given proper link. Its fibre at $t\in F_{j-1}$ is the link fibre extended to $\kappa(t)$, hence nonempty connected by hypothesis. It is thus surjective and closed, so has the quotient topology: a set with closed preimage is the image of that preimage and is closed. The connected-preimage lemma, applied to the whole connected target, proves $F_j$ connected. This holds for every $L$ and $c$, giving all the asserted fibres of $h$.

source.place: Tag 0377 (lemma-connected-fibres-quotient-topology-connected-components), with morphisms.tex Tag 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper); agent induction over the links.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$. Write $Z=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $E=W\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The natural $E\to Z$ is the base change of the assumed finite surjection $W\to Y$, hence finite surjective and continuous. If $x$ is off $N$, the complement isomorphism identifies $C\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with a single point $c=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Thus $E=W\times_C\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is nonempty connected by step 2. Its continuous surjective image $Z$ is nonempty connected: a separation of $Z$ would pull back to a separation of $E$.

If $x$ lies on $N$, it factors uniquely as $n:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to N\hookrightarrow X$, since the ideal of the closed immersion maps to zero in the field $\Omega$. Apply the geometric-fibre decomposition to $B\to N$: it is finite, hence proper, separated and quasi-compact. Its degree two gives exactly two copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, denoted $b_1,b_2$. The cartesian square in the hypotheses identifies $C\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with this fibre of $B\to N$. Base change of this finite coproduct therefore identifies $E$ with $F_1\amalg F_2$, where $F_i=W\times_{C,b_i}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Both $F_i$ are nonempty connected by step 2.

source.place: Tag 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral), cartesian square; finite etale geometric-fibre splitting: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 09Z9 (lemma-normal-scheme-with-alg-closed-function-field), assertion (1).

proof.text: The two sections $b_i$ in the marked subscheme of $W$ give points $z_i\in F_i$. Their images in $Z$ coincide: the pushout relation on $Y$ sends each marked branch to the point specified by $n$, and both projections to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ are the identity. The connected images of $F_1,F_2$ thus meet. They cover $Z$ by the surjectivity in step 3. Explicitly, in any clopen separation of $Z$, each connected image lies in one side, their common point forces the same side, and coverage makes the other side empty. Therefore $Z$ is nonempty connected.

source.place: Tag 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral), defining commutative square; elementary separation argument.

proof.text: Steps 3--5 apply to every algebraically closed geometric point of $X$. For any $x_0\in X$, apply the algebraic-closure criterion to the $\kappa(x_0)$-scheme $Y_{x_0}$: its base change to an algebraic closure is the connected nonempty $Z$ just proved. Thus every fibre of $p$ stays nonempty connected after every residue-field extension. Finally $p_{\bar s}:Y_{\bar s}\to X_{\bar s}$ is proper; its fibres are residue-field extensions of fibres of $p$, so are nonempty connected. It is a closed surjection and therefore quotient. If $X_{\bar s}$ is nonempty connected, the connected-preimage lemma gives nonempty connected $Y_{\bar s}$. For $B=N=\varnothing$ only the off-$N$ case occurs. For $m=0$ the induction is its base case. No total space or intermediate fibre was assumed connected.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q133-6eecf3b88 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First split of Q02's node, not a 2026-10-21 re-split (no repair note). Statement and stmt_deps are the same as live/side-live, and there are no new nodes. I read all six steps against the cited statements; every one holds. Step 1: composition gives h proper, projectivity gives X and Y proper over S, and proper-over-separated (01W6(2)) gives p proper. Step 2: induction on F_j = V_j×_C Spec L with base F_0 = Spec L. Each map is a base change of a proper link, hence a closed surjection with nonempty connected fibres and so a quotient map; the 0377 node then gives F_j connected. This proves geometric connectedness of the fibres of h. Step 3: E = W×_Y Z, so E→Z is finite surjective by 01WL and 01S1. Off N, the cartesian square and the complement isomorphism give C×_XΩ = Spec Ω, so E = W×_CΩ is connected. Step 4: x factors through N. Applied to B→N, the first clause of the etale-geometric-fibre node (checked against 09Z9(1), etale-cohomology.tex:14312) gives two sheets because the degree is 2, and coproduct base change gives E = F_1⊔F_2. Step 5 is genuinely elementary: the marked points z_i = (i_W b_i, id) have the same image (j_N n, id) by the pushout relation and h i_W = i_C. The two connected images meet and cover Z. Step 6: the algebraic-closure criterion (0387/054N) gives p geometrically connected fibres. p_s̄ is a proper surjection with connected fibres, so 0377 gives Y_s̄ connected. Edge cases checked: m=0, B=N=∅, two P^1's pinched at one point, contracted trees, non-closed x, characteristic 2. Unused hypotheses (flatness, nodality, trait, smooth loci, pushouts surviving geometric base change) are kept, so no target is weakened. No SGA. Accepted tool uses: projective-implies-proper, the first clause of the etale-geometric-fibre node, and the algebraic-closure test. Batch-5 flag on lem-sfb-etale-geometric-fibre-compact-sections: the only sec-trace-formula node its closure reaches is the general definition def-trf-schematically-dense-open (through its H^0_c clause). The step uses only the generic fact that an étale geometric fibre is a finite disjoint union of points, which is neither trace formula nor Poincaré duality nor part of their proofs, so the citation stands. Minor: the report mentions a citations.json the commit does not contain; this is not a fault. No fixes.
